minutes.headline: Finance Committee edited financial policies, then voted on recommendations for 18 special Town Meeting articles.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the town financial policies: levy wording, free cash priorities, stabilization funds, the investment policy and the OPEB policy. It then held a public hearing on the November 13 special Town Meeting warrant and voted to recommend some articles and to wait on others.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to strike all dedicated stabilization funds from the town's stabilization policy.
It approved revised free cash priority sections and changed the levy wording to the prior levy plus an increase allowed by Proposition 2½.
The committee changed the levy wording to refer to an increase allowed by Proposition 2½.
At the public hearing on the November 13 special Town Meeting warrant, it heard a budget adjustment article using excess revenue and new growth.
Other warrant items covered a DPW union contract paid from the salary reserve and a bond premium used to reduce pavement management borrowing.

why_it_matters: The financial policies guide how the town uses free cash and stabilization money, which affects how much is set aside for future needs and how much is left to offset tax bills.
The warrant articles the committee weighed, including a union contract and road borrowing, are the ones residents will be asked to vote on at the November 13 special Town Meeting.
